A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 15-page versions of IMPACT. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation, including accuracy, model size, throughput, and memory results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix B, including benchmark accuracies and inference measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same objective, gradient-informed activation weighting, eigenvector selection, profiling procedure, and compressed-layer construction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate mathematical reasoning on GSM8K and MATH and code generation on HumanEval and MBPP. No training or evaluation coverage is added, removed, or revised.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SVD, FWSVD, and AFM as low-rank baselines, and standard 4-bit quantization, 4-bit QLoRA, and 8-bit FLAP in the quantization experiments.

E3.justification: Both retain the same 7B/13B Llama 2 and CodeLlama models, finetuning–compression–finetuning sequence, Pass@1 evaluations, quantization configurations, and throughput and memory measurements.

E4.justification: The activation-gradient analysis in Figure 1 and inference-efficiency analysis in Section 4.5 are unchanged. No ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness tests, or case studies are added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or result error bars. Uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and Figures 1–8 retain the same result entries, numerical values, and trends, including compression–accuracy comparisons and throughput and memory findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorems 1–5, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Differences in extracted mathematical spacing do not correspond to substantive revisions.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an importance-aware activation-reconstruction framework, a closed-form eigenvector solution, and up to 48.6% greater model size reduction at comparable accuracy.

C2.justification: The explanations of activation sensitivity, quantization benefits, and inference efficiency remain unchanged. No substantive limitations, failure conditions, or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the experimental sections provide the same profiling, implementation, and evaluation details. No technical settings or code/data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and positioning relative to weight-based and activation-based compression, including the same novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 adds equal-contribution markers for Md Mokarram Chowdhury and Yang Li and identifies Yang Li as corresponding author with an email address. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added author footnotes slightly reflow the introduction across the first two pages. Figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies author contributions and correspondence, with limited accompanying layout changes. The scientific exposition, experimental evidence, theoretical derivations, and reproducibility information are unchanged, yielding no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
